title: Home & House
description: Learn to describe your home, talk about rooms and furniture, use prepositions of place to describe where things are, and understand your living space in Spanish.

grammar.title: Prepositions of Place
grammar.content:
Prepositions of place tell you WHERE something is located.

en = in/on (general location)
sobre = on/above
debajo de = under/below
entre = between
junto a = next to
al lado de = next to
al lado de = beside
detrás de = behind
delante de = in front of
cerca de = near
lejos de = far from
dentro de = inside of
fuera de = outside of
encima de = on top of

Usage tips:
- 'en' is the most common and versatile preposition
- 'sobre' and 'encima de' both mean 'on top of', but 'sobre' can also mean 'above'
- 'dentro de' emphasizes being inside something enclosed
- 'fuera de' is used for being outside something
examples:
El libro está en la mesa. (The book is on the table.)
El gato está debajo de la silla. (The cat is under the chair.)
La lámpara está sobre la mesa. (The lamp is on the table.)
El perro está detrás de la puerta. (The dog is behind the door.)
La flor está delante de la ventana. (The flower is in front of the window.)
El sofá está junto a la pared. (The sofa is next to the wall.)
El cuadro está encima del armario. (The picture is on top of the wardrobe.)
El jardín está al lado de la casa. (The garden is next to the house.)
Las llaves están entre los libros. (The keys are between the books.)
Está lejos de la ciudad. (It is far from the city.)

grammar.title: Hay — There is / There are
grammar.content:
Hay is the impersonal form of the verb 'haber'. It means 'there is' or 'there are' in English.

Key rule: 'hay' does NOT change for singular or plural.

Positive: hay (there is / there are)
Negative: no hay (there is not / there are not)
Question: ¿hay...? (is there...? / are there...?)

When used with numbers:
Hay + number + noun (plural)
Hay dos dormitorios. (There are two bedrooms.)

When used with quantifiers:
Hay mucho/a = there is/are a lot of
Hay poco/a = there is/are a little/few
Hay mucho + singular noun (there is a lot of)
Hay muchos/muchas + plural noun (there are many)

Common expressions:
¿Hay...? = Is there...? / Are there...?
No hay = There is/are not
Hay que + infinitive = one must / it is necessary to (note: different meaning from 'hay')
examples:
Hay un baño en el apartamento. (There is a bathroom in the apartment.)
Hay dos dormitorios en la casa. (There are two bedrooms in the house.)
Hay muchos muebles en el salón. (There are many pieces of furniture in the living room.)
No hay televisor en el dormitorio. (There is no television in the bedroom.)
¿Hay agua caliente? (Is there hot water?)
No hay agua caliente en el baño. (There is no hot water in the bathroom.)
Hay mucha gente en el jardín. (There are many people in the garden.)
Hay poca luz en el estudio. (There is little light in the study.)

grammar.title: Tener — To Have
grammar.content:
Tener means 'to have'. It is a regular -ER verb with a stem change (e->ie) in the present tense.

Conjugation (present tense):
Yo tengo (I have)
Tú tienes (you have informal)
Él/Ella/Usted tiene (he/she/you formal has)
Nosotros tenemos (we have)
Vosotros tenéis (you all have — Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes tienen (they/you all have)

Note: 'tengo' is irregular — the 'g' is added.

Common expressions with tener:
- tener una casa/apartamento = to have a house/apartment
- tener habitaciones = to have rooms
- tener muebles = to have furniture
- tener calefacción = to have heating
- tener un jardín = to have a garden
- tener una terraza = to have a terrace
- tener dos baños = to have two bathrooms

Negative: no tener = to not have
¿Tienes...? = Do you have...?

Other common 'tener' expressions:
- tener hambre = to be hungry (literally 'to have hunger')
- tener sed = to be thirsty (literally 'to have thirst')
- tener calor = to be hot (literally 'to have heat')
- tener frío = to be cold (literally 'to have cold')
- tener sueño = to be sleepy (literally 'to have sleep')
- tener prisa = to be in a hurry (literally 'to have hurry')
- tener razón = to be right (literally 'to have reason')
examples:
Tengo una casa grande. (I have a big house.)
Tienes dos dormitorios. (You have two bedrooms.)
Él tiene un apartamento pequeño. (He has a small apartment.)
Nosotros tenemos un jardín bonito. (We have a beautiful garden.)
No tengo calefacción. (I don't have heating.)
¿Tienes un baño privado? (Do you have a private bathroom?)
Tengo hambre. (I am hungry.)
Tengo frío en el dormitorio. (I am cold in the bedroom.)
Tienen dos baños. (They have two bathrooms.)

grammar.title: Ser and Estar — To Be (Descriptions)
grammar.content:
Spanish has TWO verbs for 'to be': SER and ESTAR. Both are used for descriptions but in different contexts.

SER is used for:
- Permanent or inherent characteristics
- Identity (what something IS)
- Material, origin, time
- Describing the house itself (size, type, style)

Estar is used for:
- Location (where something IS)
- Temporary conditions
- Feelings and states
- Describing how something currently IS

Conjugation — SER:
Yo soy (I am)
Tú eres (you are informal)
Él/Ella/Usted es (he/she/you formal is)
Nosotros somos (we are)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes son (they/you all are)

Conjugation — ESTAR:
Yo estoy (I am)
Tú estás (you are informal)
Él/Ella/Usted está (he/she/you formal is)
Nosotros estamos (we are)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes están (they/you all are)

Using SER for home descriptions:
La casa es grande. (The house is big.) — inherent characteristic
La casa es moderna. (The house is modern.) — type/style
El apartamento es pequeño. (The apartment is small.)
La casa es de ladrillo. (The house is made of brick.) — material

Using ESTAR for home descriptions:
La casa está limpia. (The house is clean.) — temporary state
La casa está sucia. (The house is dirty.)
El salón está ordenado. (The living room is tidy.)
La cocina está sucia. (The kitchen is dirty.)

Using ESTAR for location:
La mesa está en el salón. (The table is in the living room.)
El sofá está junto a la ventana. (The sofa is next to the window.)
La casa está en el centro. (The house is in the center.)
examples:
Mi casa es grande y moderna. (My house is big and modern.)
Mi apartamento es pequeño pero bonito. (My apartment is small but pretty.)
La casa está limpia hoy. (The house is clean today.)
El dormitorio está ordenado. (The bedroom is tidy.)
La cocina está sucia después de cocinar. (The kitchen is dirty after cooking.)
La mesa está en el comedor. (The table is in the dining room.)
La lámpara está sobre la mesa. (The lamp is on the table.)
El sofá está frente a la televisión. (The sofa is opposite the television.)

grammar.title: Demonstrative Adjectives — This/That/Those
grammar.content:
Demonstrative adjectives point out specific nouns. They must agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.

Near (this/these — close to speaker):
este/esta (this — singular)
estos/estas (these — plural)

Medium distance (that/those — close to listener):
eso/esesa → ese/esa (that — singular)
esos/esas (those — plural)

Far from both (that over there/those over there):
aquel/aquella (that over there — singular)
aquellos/aquellas (those over there — plural)

Agreement examples:
este libro (this book — m, singular)
esta casa (this house — f, singular)
estos muebles (these pieces of furniture — m, plural)
estas sillas (these chairs — f, plural)

Using them with home vocabulary:
este dormitorio (this bedroom)
esta silla (this chair)
estos muebles (these pieces of furniture)
ese armario (that wardrobe — closer to listener)
esa mesa (that table)
aquella casa (that house over there)
aquel jardín (that garden over there)

Note: demonstratives don't usually have accent marks in modern Spanish (real Academia rules changed in 2010).
examples:
Esta casa es bonita. (This house is pretty.)
Este dormitorio es grande. (This bedroom is big.)
Estas sillas son viejas. (These chairs are old.)
Ese sofá es cómodo. (That sofa is comfortable.)
Esas cortinas son bonitas. (Those curtains are pretty.)
Aquella casa tiene un jardín. (That house over there has a garden.)
Aquel armario es antiguo. (That wardrobe over there is antique.)
Estos muebles son de madera. (These pieces of furniture are made of wood.)

grammar.title: Describing Your Home — Sentence Patterns
grammar.content:
Useful sentence patterns for talking about your home:

Basic description:
Mi casa es [adjective]. (My house is [adjective].)
Mi casa tiene [number] habitaciones. (My house has [number] rooms.)
Mi casa está en [location]. (My house is in [location].)

Rooms:
En la [room] hay [furniture/object]. (In the [room] there is [furniture].)
En mi [room] hay una [object]. (In my [room] there is a [object].)
Mi [room] es [adjective]. (My [room] is [adjective].)

Furniture and objects:
[Object] está [preposition] [location]. (The [object] is [preposition] [location].)
El/La [object] es [adjective]. (The [object] is [adjective].)

Combining ideas:
Mi casa es grande y tiene tres dormitorios.
En la cocina hay una mesa y cuatro sillas.
En el salón hay un sofá grande frente a la televisión.
El dormitorio principal es muy luminoso.
Mi apartamento está en el centro de la ciudad.
Tengo un jardín pequeño detrás de la casa.

Useful adjectives:
grande = big
diminuto/a = tiny
cómodo/a = comfortable
incómodo/a = uncomfortable
luminoso/a = bright
curioso/a = dark
bonito/a = pretty
feo/a = ugly
antiguo/a = old (antique)
nuevo/a = new
limpio/a = clean
sucio/a = dirty
ordenado/a = tidy
desordenado/a = messy
pequeño/a = small
amplio/a = spacious

Questions:
¿Cuántas habitaciones tiene tu casa? (How many rooms does your house have?)
¿Dónde está el baño? (Where is the bathroom?)
¿Qué hay en el salón? (What is in the living room?)
¿Es grande tu casa? (Is your house big?)
¿Tienes jardín? (Do you have a garden?)
examples:
Mi casa es grande y luminosa. (My house is big and bright.)
Mi casa tiene tres dormitorios y dos baños. (My house has three bedrooms and two bathrooms.)
En la cocina hay una nevera y un horno. (In the kitchen there is a fridge and an oven.)
En el salón hay un sofá frente a la televisión. (In the living room there is a sofa opposite the TV.)
El dormitorio es muy cómodo. (The bedroom is very comfortable.)
Mi apartamento está en el segundo piso. (My apartment is on the second floor.)
Tengo una terraza pequeña. (I have a small terrace.)

exercises.question: What is 'kitchen' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Cocina' = kitchen. 'Salón' = living room. 'Baño' = bathroom. 'Dormitorio' = bedroom.

exercises.question: How do you say 'there is/are' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Hay' = there is/are. 'Es' = is (identity, from ser). 'Está' = is (location, from estar). 'Tiene' = has.

exercises.question: What does 'debajo de' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Debajo de' = under/below. 'Sobre' = on. 'Detrás de' = behind. 'Delante de' = in front of.

exercises.question: Complete: ___ un libro en la mesa. (There is a book on the table.)
exercises.explanation: 'Hay' = there is. 'Hay un libro' = There is a book.

exercises.question: Complete: El gato está ___ la silla. (The cat is under the chair.)
exercises.explanation: 'Debajo de' = under/below.

exercises.question: Complete: Mi casa ___ grande. (My house is big.)
exercises.explanation: Use SER for permanent characteristics: 'Mi casa es grande' (My house is big — it's a permanent quality).

exercises.question: What is 'bedroom' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Dormitorio' = bedroom. 'Cocina' = kitchen. 'Baño' = bathroom. 'Salón' = living room.

exercises.question: Complete: La mesa está ___ la ventana. (The table is in front of the window.)
exercises.explanation: 'Delante de' = in front of.

exercises.question: What does 'junto a' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Junto a' = next to. 'Detrás de' = behind. 'Entre' = between. 'Lejos de' = far from.

exercises.question: Complete: No ___ un sofá en el salón. (There is no sofa in the living room.)
exercises.explanation: 'No hay' = there is not. 'No hay un sofá' = There is no sofa.

exercises.question: What is 'wardrobe' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Armario' = wardrobe/closet. 'Estantería' = bookshelf. 'Mesilla' = nightstand. 'Cómoda' = chest of drawers.

exercises.question: Complete: ___ tengo una casa grande. (I have a big house.)
exercises.explanation: 'Yo tengo' = I have. 'Tengo' is the first person singular of 'tener' (to have).

exercises.question: Complete: La casa está ___ (clean).
exercises.explanation: 'Limpia' = clean. 'La casa está limpia' = The house is clean. Use ESTAR for temporary states like cleanliness.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'The book is on the table'
exercises.correct: el libro está en la mesa
exercises.explanation: 'El libro' = the book. 'Está' = is (location). 'En la mesa' = on the table.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'There are two bedrooms'
exercises.explanation: 'Hay' = there are. 'Dos' = two. 'Dormitorios' = bedrooms. 'Hay' doesn't change for plural.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'I have a big garden'
exercises.explanation: 'Tengo' = I have. 'Un jardín' = a garden. 'Grande' = big. In Spanish, adjectives usually come AFTER the noun.

exercises.question: What is 'bathroom' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Baño' = bathroom. 'Cocina' = kitchen. 'Dormitorio' = bedroom. 'Comedor' = dining room.

exercises.question: Which verb do you use to describe where something is located?
exercises.explanation: Use ESTAR for location: 'La mesa está en el salón' (The table is in the living room). SER is for identity/permanent traits.

exercises.question: Complete: ___ casa es nueva. (My house is new.)
exercises.explanation: 'Mi' = my. 'Mi casa es nueva' = My house is new. 'Nueva' is feminine to agree with 'casa'.

exercises.question: Complete: El perro está ___ la puerta. (The dog is behind the door.)
exercises.explanation: 'Detrás de' = behind.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'The sofa is next to the wall'
exercises.correct: el sofá está junto a la pared
exercises.explanation: 'El sofá' = the sofa. 'Está' = is. 'Junto a' = next to. 'La pared' = the wall.

exercises.question: What does 'encima de' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Encima de' = on top of. 'Debajo de' = under. 'Entre' = between. 'Cerca de' = near.

exercises.question: Complete: La cocina tiene un ___ y un horno. (The kitchen has a fridge and an oven.)
exercises.explanation: 'Nevera' = fridge. 'La cocina tiene una nevera' = The kitchen has a fridge. Note: 'nevera' is feminine so it's 'una nevera'.

exercises.question: Complete: ___ casa está en el centro. (My house is in the center.)
exercises.explanation: 'Mi' = my. 'Mi casa está en el centro' = My house is in the center. Use ESTAR for location.

exercises.question: What is 'window' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Ventana' = window. 'Puerta' = door. 'Pared' = wall. 'Techo' = ceiling.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'Do you have a garden?'
exercises.explanation: '¿Tienes' = do you have (informal, tú form of tener). 'Un jardín' = a garden. In Spanish, questions use inverted question marks.

exercises.question: Which demonstrative means 'this' (close to speaker) for a feminine noun?
exercises.explanation: 'Esta' = this (feminine singular, close to speaker). 'Ese' = that (masculine). 'Aquel' = that over there. 'Esos' = those (masculine plural).

exercises.question: Complete: Este ___ es muy cómodo. (This sofa is very comfortable.)
exercises.explanation: 'Sofá' = sofa (masculine). 'Este sofá' = this sofa. 'Ese' would be used for something further away.

exercises.question: Translate to Spanish: 'The cat is under the bed'
exercises.correct: el gato está debajo de la cama
exercises.explanation: 'El gato' = the cat. 'Está' = is. 'Debajo de' = under. 'La cama' = the bed.

exercises.question: What is 'ceiling' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Techo' = ceiling. 'Suelo' = floor. 'Pared' = wall. 'Puerta' = door.

exercises.question: Complete: En el baño hay una ___ y una bañera. (In the bathroom there is a shower and a bathtub.)
exercises.explanation: 'Ducha' = shower. 'En el baño hay una ducha' = In the bathroom there is a shower.
